question: I went to Virtue restaurant & bar in Chicago for my birthday on March 22, 2021 and the main course I had was delicious!  Unfortunately, when I went back about a month later on April 21, it was no longer on the dinner menu.  Using the Wayback Machine, can you help me figure out which main course was on the dinner menu for Virtue on March 22, 2021 but not April 21, 2021? Answer using the singular form, without articles.

history.name: user
history.content: I went to Virtue restaurant & bar in Chicago for my birthday on March 22, 2021 and the main course I had was delicious! history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Understood. We'll use the Wayback Machine to compare Virtue’s dinner menu around March 22, 2021 and April 21, 2021. Team: WebSurfer (browser), FileSurfer (files), Assistant (coordination). Plan: find March 2021 snapshot near 3/22, list dinner mains; find April 2021 near 4/21, list dinner mains; identify the dish present in March and missing in April; answer in singular without articles.

history.content: Click Menus and then go to the Dinner section.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Menus page loaded. Sections: Dinner, Brunch, Dessert, Beverages. Clicking Dinner anchor. Some content tiles are loading; a few images failed due to archived asset blocking. Text headers visible.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: List the main courses visible under Dinner for this March 19 snapshot.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Visible Dinner mains (text areas rendered, a couple image tiles show broken icons):
- Catfish
- Short rib
- Fried chicken
- Pork chop
Note: There are placeholders suggesting at least one more item might be present but not rendering. Some entries show partial text; asset loading appears incomplete.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Check whether there’s a snapshot specifically on March 22, 2021. If available, open it and confirm the Dinner mains.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Opened snapshot timestamped March 22, 2021. Dinner section loads similarly. Visible mains match prior list: Catfish, Short rib, Fried chicken, Pork chop. One tile shows a generic "market fish" image placeholder with no text; possibly a rotating fish option. Text for a potential fifth item isn’t fully visible due to CSS/JS not loading completely.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Now open a snapshot closest to April 21, 2021 and list the Dinner mains there.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Opened snapshot from April 21, 2021. Dinner section shows:
- Short rib
- Fried chicken
- Pork chop
- Trout (or listed as "market fish: trout")
Catfish isn’t visible here. There may be a missing tile due to styling; however, the visible fish entry is trout, not catfish.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Compare the March 22 mains to April 21 mains and state the differences.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: March 22 (visible): Catfish, Short rib, Fried chicken, Pork chop (+ possibly one more partially rendered). April 21 (visible): Short rib, Fried chicken, Pork chop, Trout. Difference observed: Catfish appears in March but not April, replaced by trout/market fish.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Given the observed difference, the main course present on March 22 but not on April 21 is catfish. I’ll proceed with that answer.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Quickly check if there’s any Dinner PDF or alternate menu format on the archived site for March that explicitly lists mains, just to confirm.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Attempted to open a linked PDF in the menu page; the archived link returns a 404 due to asset capture issues. No alternate text-only version found. The visible text tiles still show Catfish among mains in March; April shows Trout instead.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Understood. Let's proceed with the earlier conclusion.

history.name: FileSurfer
history.content: I attempted to extract innerText from the archived HTML of the Dinner section. The text yields: "Catfish", "Short rib", "Fried chicken", "Pork chop". Several divs are empty or contain ARIA attributes without text. This appears incomplete due to missing CSS/JS, but Catfish is explicitly present in March extracts.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Alright. Even with partial rendering, we have Catfish visible in March and not in April.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: For a loose cross-check, I looked at Virtue’s Instagram posts around March 2021. Saw a caption referencing "fried catfish" dinner special mid-March. Not definitive, but aligns with Catfish being a main in March.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Noted. While social posts aren’t authoritative, the menu tiles we saw already indicate Catfish.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Checked Instagram posts around late April 2021—saw a photo caption referencing "trout" or "market fish". This matches the April menu’s fish entry and supports Catfish being rotated off.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Summary so far: March shows Catfish among mains; April shows Trout (market fish), and Catfish is absent. The removed dish appears to be Catfish.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Open an April snapshot on April 23, 2021 to confirm Catfish absence once more.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Opened April 23, 2021 snapshot. Dinner mains visible: Short rib, Fried chicken, Pork chop, Trout. No Catfish visible.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Open another March snapshot (e.g., March 18) to confirm Catfish presence.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Opened March 18, 2021 snapshot. Dinner section shows Catfish, Short rib, Fried chicken, Pork chop. One tile still shows a broken image; the text for that slot isn’t visible.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: This strengthens the observation: Catfish present in mid-March snapshots, not present in late April.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Agreed. Catfish is the difference we’re looking for.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Thanks. Despite minor rendering gaps, we have enough to proceed.

history.name: FileSurfer
history.content: Note: The archived CSS appears broken, which can hide or truncate some text items. I cannot recover the missing tile text without JS assets.

mistake_reason: At step 17, Assistant accepted WebSurfer’s incomplete and partially rendered menu data as definitive and decided the answer was 'catfish' without asking for clarification or requesting a full, verified list of mains. Despite explicit signs of missing tiles and broken assets (ambiguous/incomplete data), Assistant failed to seek additional confirmation or instruct the team to load alternate snapshots or sources to ensure accuracy, exemplifying FM-2.2 (Fail to Ask for Clarification). This premature decision anchored the team on an incorrect conclusion and led to the wrong final answer.
